S6.01.note: Palettes are defined per theme in apps/cli/src/tui/terminal_palette.rs (PALETTE_DARK, PALETTE_LIGHT, etc.).
steps: Start agi and type /theme, then press Enter.
Press the down arrow until Light is highlighted; the screen previews it live.
Press Enter to confirm Light.
Compare the page background and panel backgrounds with the previous theme. Expected: the whole screen repaints from the named theme colours, not per component.
S6.01.where: Type /theme in the TUI, then pick Light and press Enter

S6.02.note: The cited code also uses the elevated surface in model_picker.rs and approval_overlay.rs; only the theme popup was checked by eye.
steps: Start agi and type /theme, then press Enter.
Look at the popup box titled Theme over the chat.
Compare its background with the chat area behind it.
Expected: the popup uses a raised surface colour that differs from the page ground.
S6.02.where: Type /theme; the popup titled Theme is the raised surface

S6.03.needs: a model account that can answer, so a reply appears
S6.03.note: Text colours are named tokens in apps/cli/src/tui/terminal_palette.rs; contrast is not measured in the cited code paths.
steps: Type /theme, pick a theme with the arrow keys, and press Enter.
Read a chat reply in that theme.
Repeat for Dark, Light and High Contrast Light.
Expected: primary and muted text stay readable on every background. A 4.5:1 ratio cannot be read by eye.
S6.03.where: Chat text in any theme, after /theme

S6.04.needs: a model account that can answer (for the table step)
S6.04.note: The cited code uses one muted border colour (ui_muted); no separate subtle and strong border tokens were found.
steps: Type /theme and press Enter.
Look at the border of the Theme popup.
Ask for a reply that contains a Markdown table and look at its border lines.
Expected: borders use a named border colour per theme.
S6.04.where: Type /theme; the popup border and the table borders in a reply

steps: Type /theme and press Enter.
Press the down arrow to move the highlight to another theme.
Look at the highlighted row: it has a coloured fill with dark text.
Look at the row marked as the current theme: its name is bold in the accent colour.
Expected: fill, text and on-fill colours are separate roles and each is readable.
S6.05.where: Type /theme, then move the highlight with the arrow keys

S6.06.note: The colour role used for this message was not checked in code; the success, warning, danger and info tokens are in apps/cli/src/tui/terminal_palette.rs.
steps: Type /theme nosuchtheme and press Enter.
Read the message: Unknown theme with the list of available themes.
Switch to Light with /theme light and compare the colour of the message.
Expected: success, warning, error and info text each have their own colour and read clearly in both light and dark themes.
S6.06.where: Status messages in the chat, for example after /theme with a wrong name

S6.08.needs: a model account that can answer
S6.08.note: A terminal has no font size or line-height, so the scale is colour, weight and underline only.
steps: Ask agi for a reply that contains a level 1 and a level 2 heading (for example, a short Markdown outline).
Compare level 1 (accent colour, bold, underlined) with level 2 (accent colour, bold).
Expected: each heading level has a fixed style that repeats across replies.

S6.10.needs: a model account that can answer and a tool action
S6.10.note: A terminal does not set a font size, so the 12px rule cannot be checked from the code; only the muted colour role was found.
steps: Ask agi to run a simple tool action so a tool row appears.
Look at the summary text under the tool row.
Expected: metadata uses the muted text colour, at a size no smaller than 12px.
S6.10.where: Metadata lines in the chat, such as the summary text under a tool row

S6.11.needs: a model account that can answer
S6.11.note: The CLI does not declare a monospace font family; the terminal's own font applies to all text. Not verified beyond the cited code.
steps: Ask agi for a reply that includes a short code block.
Compare the code lines with the normal paragraph text.
Expected: code is set apart by its frame and colours, using monospace text from the terminal.
S6.11.where: Code blocks in a chat reply

S6.13.needs: a model account that can answer
steps: Ask agi for a reply with two or three separate paragraphs.
Look at the blank line between paragraphs.
Expected: the gap between paragraphs is the same everywhere.
S6.13.where: Two paragraphs in one chat reply

S6.14.needs: a model account that can answer
S6.14.note: The indent rule is in apps/cli/src/tui/markdown_renderer.rs near line 306, not at the cited line 157, which has moved.
steps: Ask agi for a reply with a bulleted list that has a nested sub-list.
Look at the bullet indent for the first level and the nested level.
Expected: each nesting level indents by the same step.
S6.14.where: Bulleted and nested lists in a chat reply

S6.15.needs: a model account that can answer
steps: Ask agi for a reply with a short code block.
Look at the frame above the code and the left bar beside each code line.
Expected: the code block has the same internal padding every time.
S6.15.where: Code blocks in a chat reply

S6.16.needs: a model account that can answer
S6.16.note: The cited line 300 no longer holds table code; table layout is near apps/cli/src/tui/markdown_renderer.rs lines 462 to 470.
steps: Ask agi for a reply that contains a table with several columns.
Look at the spacing inside each cell.
Expected: cells have the same padding in every column.
S6.16.where: A Markdown table in a chat reply

S6.17.needs: a model account that can answer and a tool action
S6.17.note: The cited code (tui_app.rs around line 463) adds a blank line before a tool row unless it follows another tool row; it does not set a separate turn gap.
steps: Send two or three messages that each run a tool action.
Look at the blank line before each tool row.
Expected: the gap between turns uses one spacing value.
S6.17.where: Between chat turns and tool rows in the TUI chat

S6.19.note: The continuation indent is set by the prompt width in apps/cli/src/tui/tui_app.rs (render_input).
steps: Start agi and type a long line that wraps to a second row.
Look at the wrapped row: it should line up after the prompt character.
Expected: the input and its prompt have a defined inner padding.
S6.19.where: The input line at the bottom of the TUI (the composer)

S6.20.needs: a model account that can answer
S6.20.note: A test in apps/cli/src/tui/tui_app.rs checks the left gutter; no rule that steps the gutter with width was found.
steps: Make the terminal window narrow.
Ask for a reply with a long line of text, or send a long message.
Look at the left edge of the wrapped rows.
Expected: the text keeps a left margin and does not touch the terminal edge.
S6.20.where: Long wrapped text in the TUI chat when the window is narrow

S6.23.note: Padding was checked only in the theme popup; other dialogs were not compared.
steps: Type /theme and press Enter.
Look at the gap between the popup border and its first row, and between the border and the preview text.
Compare the padding on the left and right sides.
S6.23.where: Type /theme; the popup has one inner padding

S6.30.needs: a model account that can answer
S6.30.note: No easing curves were found; the sweep is linear and time-based.
steps: Send a message that makes agi work for a few seconds.
Watch the spinner beside the status text, which turns through frames.
Watch the highlight that moves across the status text.
Expected: the motion uses fixed durations (a frame every 50 ms, a sweep every 2 seconds).
S6.30.where: The status line while agi is working in the TUI

S6.31.needs: a model account that can answer, so the spinner shows
S6.31.note: Only the agi setting and plain output turn reduced motion on; the operating-system Reduce Motion setting is not read.
steps: Type /config set reduced-motion true and press Enter.
Send a message that makes agi work, and watch the spinner: it shows a still dot instead of turning frames.
Watch the status text: the moving highlight should stop.
Type /config show and check the line Reduced motion: true.
S6.31.where: Type /config set reduced-motion true in the TUI, then /config show

S6.32.needs: none (a model account for the code block step)
S6.32.note: Auto follows the terminal background colour (terminal_is_light), not the macOS appearance setting; it falls back to Dark if the background cannot be read.
steps: Type /theme and press Enter.
Move to Auto (described as Match the terminal background) and press Enter.
Move to Light and press Enter.
Look at the whole screen, including a code block in a reply: all of it should follow the chosen theme.
S6.32.where: Type /theme and pick Auto, Dark or Light

S6.33.note: No operating-system high-contrast setting is read; the treatment is a separate palette, and no separate focus-ring style was found.
steps: Type /theme and press Enter.
Move to High Contrast Dark and press Enter.
Compare the text, the popup border and the highlighted row with the Dark theme.
Expected: text, borders and focus look stronger than in Dark.
S6.33.where: Type /theme and pick High Contrast Dark or High Contrast Light

S6.34.note: No pressed or disabled style was found in the theme picker; the cited tui_app.rs line 1662 is approval-timing code.
steps: Type /theme and press Enter.
Press the down arrow: the row under the cursor gets an accent fill with dark bold text.
Look at the current theme: its name is bold in the accent colour, while the other rows are plain.
Expected: selected, focused and active rows look different; hovered, pressed and disabled states are not present in a terminal.
S6.34.where: Type /theme, then move with the arrow keys
